project.commit_note: The exact staged vulnerable source reviewed here is the prepared libavc checkout at `ea14d495b1995ff09642edfb1b0b45a3d289b0af` (`DO NOT MERGE - Merge Android 10 into master`, 2019-09-04); its line map matches the saved AddressSanitizer stack (`ih264_inter_pred_luma_horz_hpel_vert_qpel_ssse3:3683`, `ih264d_motion_compensate_mp:1125`, `ih264d_parse_bslice:1687`, `ih264d_free_dynamic_bufs:2252`, `ih264d_init_decoder:964`). ARVO metadata separately reports `1670387156fa7d8d605c5ca8dae9824e1ee2ce0a` / `3716098904f682e57e77df98c1ed64bd33ecaf78`, but those commits are not ancestors of the staged checkout and the staged `patch.diff` is the unrelated PREUPLOAD-hook change from `3716098904f682e57e77df98c1ed64bd33ecaf78`. Local history in the staged libavc repository contains commit `74d0b8a0125460b8e2ecdd6d6995d165ded36140` (`decoder: Move initialization of dbp_mgr entries to init_decoder()`), whose commit message explicitly describes this reset-time heap-use-after-free on resolution change and whose diff moves the missing DPB-entry reinitialization into `ih264d_init_decoder`.

analysis_state.reason: Stage 01 reproduced the AddressSanitizer heap-use-after-free, and the staged source plus local history close the reset-time root cause: `ih264d_init_decoder()` frees `pu1_pic_buf_base` without reinitializing `ps_init_dpb` / `ps_mod_dpb`. The saved crash stack independently closes retry-side reachability into `ih264d_parse_bslice -> ih264d_motion_compensate_mp -> ih264_inter_pred_luma_horz_hpel_vert_qpel_ssse3`, and ASan closes the alloc/free/use endpoints. What remains unresolved is the exact retry-side value bridge from a specific stale `ps_init_dpb` / `ps_mod_dpb` entry through the selected `ps_ref_pic_buf_lx[...]` element, its `u1_pic_buf_id` / `i1_buf_id`, and the `apv_buf_id_pic_buf_map[i1_buf_id]` slot that still pointed at freed-backed state on this witness. Because `ih264_buf_mgr_get_next_free()` chooses the lowest free id while retry-side `ih264d_create_pic_buffers()` rewrites the active map prefix, Stage 02 cannot close that local source-level transition from the staged artifacts alone. `run_flags.json` keeps runtime disambiguation disabled, so this GT remains intentionally partial rather than source-to-sink complete.

bug_description.normalized: In the staged vulnerable libavc checkout `ea14d495b1995ff09642edfb1b0b45a3d289b0af`, the attacker-controlled H.264 bitstream first drives picture-buffer allocation in `ih264d_allocate_dynamic_bufs()` / `ih264d_create_pic_buffers()` and then copies live `pic_buffer_t` state into the DPB initializer tables `ps_init_dpb` and `ps_mod_dpb`. The same `Codec::decodeFrame()` call then reports `IVD_RES_CHANGED`, so the harness executes `resetCodec()` and immediately retries the same bytes. During that reset, `ih264d_init_decoder()` frees dynamic decode buffers through `ih264d_free_dynamic_bufs()`, including `pu1_pic_buf_base`, but in this vulnerable revision it does not reinitialize `ps_init_dpb` / `ps_mod_dpb`; local fix commit `74d0b8a0125460b8e2ecdd6d6995d165ded36140` moves that missing DPB-entry initialization into `ih264d_init_decoder()` and explicitly describes the resulting reset-time heap-use-after-free on resolution change. The saved ASan stack proves the retry-side parse reaches `ih264d_parse_bslice -> ih264d_decode_recon_tfr_nmb -> ih264d_motion_compensate_mp`, and the sink-side `_mm_loadu_si128((__m128i *)(pu1_src))` read lands inside the `pu1_pic_buf_base` allocation freed during reset. The available static artifacts do not preserve which exact stale DPB slot, list-building/reordering decision, or numeric `u1_pic_buf_id` carried this witness into the retry-side `apv_buf_id_pic_buf_map[i1_buf_id]` lookup, so that final bridge remains source-grounded but not statically disambiguated.

source.description: First decoder-side parser statement that consumes the attacker-controlled NAL payload buffered from the fuzzed bitstream. The later picture-buffer allocation, DPB snapshot, resolution-change status, and retry-on-reset all derive from the bytes parsed here.
source.value_from: Stage 01 fed the saved `poc` into `avc_dec_fuzzer`, and `Codec::decodeFrame()` passed the remaining witness bytes through `dec_ip.pv_stream_buffer` / `dec_ip.u4_num_Bytes` into `ih264d_video_decode()`, which copied one Annex-B NAL payload into `pu1_bitstrm_buf` immediately before this call.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. The SSSE3 luma interpolation routine performs a 16-byte read through `pu1_src`; ASan reports that read inside the `pu1_pic_buf_base` allocation freed during reset, while the exact source-level `i1_buf_id` / map-slot derivation of `pu1_src` remains unresolved.

root_cause.description: Reset frees dynamic decode state here, but this vulnerable revision does not immediately reinitialize `ps_init_dpb` / `ps_mod_dpb` afterward. Any pre-reset `pic_buffer_t` copies still left in those tables therefore retain old `pu1_buf1/2/3` pointers across the free; local fix commit `74d0b8a0125460b8e2ecdd6d6995d165ded36140` inserts the missing DPB-entry initialization at this point.

parser_admitted.description: The saved ASan stack proves the reset did not abort early: after `Codec::decodeFrame()` retries the same bytes, the parser reaches `ih264d_parse_bslice()` and continues into `ih264d_decode_recon_tfr_nmb()` and `ih264d_motion_compensate_mp()` on the crashing path.

tainted_value_origin.description: The reset-persistent lifetime state originates when `ih264d_start_of_pic()` copies live `pic_buffer_t` contents into the DPB init/mod tables. Those copied `pu1_buf1/2/3` and `u1_pic_buf_id` fields are the kind of decoder reference state that the local fix later reinitializes on reset; the exact crash-time stale slot is not preserved by the staged artifacts.

evidence_limitations: `run_flags.json` sets `runtime_disambiguation` to `false`, so Stage 02 must stay source-grounded and may not instrument which retry-side DPB slot or numeric `i1_buf_id` fed `apv_buf_id_pic_buf_map[i1_buf_id]`.

The staged source and local fix close the reset-time stale-state bug, and the saved ASan trace closes the alloc/free/use triple, but the available artifacts do not record which exact `ps_init_dpb` / `ps_mod_dpb` element, reordering decision, `u1_pic_buf_id`, or `apv_buf_id_pic_buf_map` slot supplied the crashing retry-side reference descriptor.

`ih264_buf_mgr_get_next_free()` returns the lowest free buffer id, and retry-side `ih264d_create_pic_buffers()` rewrites the active `apv_buf_id_pic_buf_map` prefix. Those exact source facts are why this repaired GT no longer claims that the straightforward current-picture / stale-map route is statically closed on this witness.

The staged `patch.diff` and reported `fixed_commit` are unrelated PREUPLOAD-hook changes; the repair evidence used here comes from the matching local repository commit `74d0b8a0125460b8e2ecdd6d6995d165ded36140` and the staged vulnerable source.

coarse_trace.summary: The attacker-controlled NAL payload is parsed, which drives picture-buffer allocation and the first decode attempt's picture/DPB initialization.
The current `pic_buffer_t` is copied into `ps_init_dpb` and `ps_mod_dpb`, so reset-persistent DPB entries now alias the current `pu1_pic_buf_base` allocation.
The same input returns `IVD_RES_CHANGED`, so the harness resets the decoder; `ih264d_init_decoder()` frees dynamic buffers but does not clear the copied DPB entries.

On the retried B-slice path, retry-side list construction consumes `ps_init_dpb` / `ps_mod_dpb` before motion compensation. Because reset did not scrub those tables, stale pre-reset picture descriptors remain a possible source for later B-slice prediction state, although the exact slot used on this witness is not preserved.

The saved ASan stack proves the retry path reaches `ih264d_motion_compensate_mp` and then the SSSE3 luma filter, but the staged source does not close which stale `ps_ref_pic_buf_lx[...]` entry, `u1_pic_buf_id`, and `apv_buf_id_pic_buf_map[i1_buf_id]` slot produced the crashing luma pointer.

fine_trace.note: The decoder begins parsing the attacker-controlled NAL payload buffered from the fuzzed H.264 stream. The later SPS-derived allocation sizes, first-picture state, and resolution-change return all come from bytes parsed through this call.

From stream-derived frame dimensions and `u1_pic_bufs`, the decoder allocates one contiguous picture-buffer backing region and stores it as `ps_dec->pu1_pic_buf_base`. ASan's allocation stack points to this allocation.
Each `pic_buffer_t` now receives luma/chroma pointers into the step-2 backing region, and the loop also registers each descriptor in `apv_buf_id_pic_buf_map[i]` for later motion-comp lookups.

The current picture descriptor is copied into the DPB initializer tables. Together with any other pre-reset DPB copies, these tables now contain live `pic_buffer_t` state with `pu1_buf1/2/3`, `u1_pic_buf_id`, and related fields that the reset path later fails to scrub.

The same decode attempt reports `IVD_RES_CHANGED`, so the harness takes the reset path and immediately retries the same buffer. The stale DPB copies from step 4 therefore survive into a reset/retry sequence.

Root cause. Reset frees dynamic decode state here, but this vulnerable function does not reinitialize the DPB init/mod entries afterward. Local fix commit `74d0b8a0125460b8e2ecdd6d6995d165ded36140` moves the DPB-entry initialization block to this exact reset path.
Reset releases the picture-buffer backing allocation from step 2. Any uncleared DPB copies from steps 4 and 6 that still reference this region now hold dangling `pu1_buf1/2/3` pointers.

After the reset/retry, B-slice setup rebuilds reference-list state from `ps_init_dpb` / `ps_mod_dpb` before motion compensation. Because step 6 did not reinitialize those tables, stale pre-reset `pic_buffer_t` entries remain in scope here, but the staged artifacts do not identify which exact slot or optional reordering arm this witness later selected.

Retry-side B-macroblock prediction selects one concrete reference entry from `ps_ref_pic_buf_lx`. Because the staged artifacts do not preserve the crashing macroblock partition, `u1_lx`, or `i1_ref_idx1`, the exact stale list slot chosen on this witness is not recoverable.

The selected entry's `u1_pic_buf_id` is packed as the future `i1_buf_id` used by motion compensation. The next source-level use is `ps_ref_frm = ps_dec->apv_buf_id_pic_buf_map[i1_buf_id]`, but Stage 01 artifacts do not preserve the concrete `u1_pic_buf_id` / `i1_buf_id` or which map slot it indexed. Because retry-side `ih264d_create_pic_buffers()` rewrote the active map prefix, this id-to-map transition is the unresolved bridge boundary.

fine_trace.code: ps_dec->apf_inter_pred_luma[ps_pred->u1_dydx](puc_ref, pu1_dest_y, u2_ref_wd_y, u2_dst_wd, u4_ht_y, u4_wd_y, puc_pred0, ps_pred->u1_dydx);
fine_trace.note: The saved crash stack proves the retried decode reaches this interpolation call from `ih264d_motion_compensate_mp`. By this point some luma reference pointer has been materialized as `puc_ref`, but the exact source-level derivation from step 10's unresolved id-to-map bridge is not recoverable from the staged artifacts.

Sink. The SSSE3 interpolation routine performs a 16-byte read through `pu1_src`, and AddressSanitizer reports that address inside the step-7 freed picture-buffer allocation. The earlier source-level derivation of `pu1_src` from a specific retry-side `i1_buf_id` / map slot remains unresolved.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_free_context: ASan's free context is the step-7 `pu1_pic_buf_base` release reached from `Codec::resetCodec -> ih264d_reset -> ih264d_init_decoder -> ih264d_free_dynamic_bufs`. The local matching fix `74d0b8a0125460b8e2ecdd6d6995d165ded36140` changes this exact reset path by reinitializing DPB entries immediately after the free call in step 6.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: The saved crash stack matches the fine trace's use path `ih264_inter_pred_luma_horz_hpel_vert_qpel_ssse3 -> ih264d_motion_compensate_mp -> ih264d_decode_recon_tfr_nmb -> ih264d_parse_bslice`, and the saved free stack matches the trace's reset path `Codec::resetCodec -> ih264d_reset -> ih264d_init_decoder -> ih264d_free_dynamic_bufs`.
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: Partially closed. The same H.264 witness both seeds live `pic_buffer_t` state in the DPB tables and triggers the `IVD_RES_CHANGED` reset/retry path, and the saved ASan trace independently proves the retried B-slice decode reaches the SSSE3 sink with a pointer inside the step-7 freed allocation. The source-level trace intentionally stops at the unresolved `ps_ref_pic_buf_lx[...] -> u1_pic_buf_id / i1_buf_id -> apv_buf_id_pic_buf_map[i1_buf_id]` bridge instead of claiming that map transition is statically closed.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged `patch.diff` / reported fixed commit `3716098904f682e57e77df98c1ed64bd33ecaf78` do not touch this decoder path. The matching local fix in the staged repository is commit `74d0b8a0125460b8e2ecdd6d6995d165ded36140`.
sanitizer_ground_truth.evidence_note: The saved `sanitizer_trace.txt` and `reproduction_report.json` match the public issue crash state and its alloc/free/use triple. `run_flags.json` disables runtime disambiguation, so Stage 02 did not instrument which retry-side DPB slot or numeric `i1_buf_id` fed `apv_buf_id_pic_buf_map[i1_buf_id]`. Source review additionally shows that `ih264_buf_mgr_get_next_free()` returns the lowest free id and that retry-side `ih264d_create_pic_buffers()` rewrites the active map prefix, so the repaired fine trace stops at that unresolved id-to-map boundary and anchors the crash site itself from the saved ASan evidence.

format.name: H.264 Annex B elementary stream for avc_dec_fuzzer
format.contract: The staged witness is the exact saved H.264 bitstream from OSS-Fuzz issue 18595. Its verified trigger semantics are limited to what the saved artifacts prove: within one `Codec::decodeFrame()` call, the decoder first reports `IVD_RES_CHANGED`, so the harness executes `resetCodec()` and retries the same bytes, and the retried parse reaches `ih264d_parse_bslice -> ih264d_decode_recon_tfr_nmb -> ih264d_motion_compensate_mp`, ending in `AddressSanitizer: heap-use-after-free READ 16` at `_mm_loadu_si128((__m128i *)(pu1_src))`. The staged artifacts do not statically prove which individual SPS-difference check fired, which exact stale DPB slot / `u1_pic_buf_id` closed the retry-side motion-comp bridge, or a broader class of H.264 streams beyond that witnessed reset-then-B-slice sequence.
